posture: Inform — the scan is no longer running clean: two fresh community-benefit signals cleared the bar in the 24 hours to Tuesday morning, both in the Social Licence & Community lens and both positive engagement moves rather than risk escalations. First, EnergyCo has opened formal consultation on the New England REZ's own $60 million Community and Employment Benefit Program (an online survey, a webinar and community sessions through July and August, with the legacy money brought forward so projects can begin before REZ construction starts), reported by the New England Times on the morning of 27 July — the New England analogue of the South West $60m program logged on 25 July, and a notable move because it lands in the state's most politically contested zone. Second, ACEREZ has confirmed Round 2 of its Central-West Orana Community Grants Program will open on 10 August with roughly $1.9 million available (small grants of $3,000-$50,000 and significant grants of $50,000-$1 million for not-for-profits, Aboriginal organisations, councils and volunteer groups) — a never-before-logged item carried once for the archive; its report date sits a few days back, just outside the strict 24-hour window, so it is treated as an inform signal rather than breaking news. Two threads that surfaced prominently in the scan resolve to stale material and are dropped: the raising of the first 70-metre 500kV transmission tower in the Central-West Orana REZ dates to 2 April 2026, and EnergyCo's EPBC/federal-approval referral for the New England transmission backbone belongs to the standing approvals thread already reflected in the digest's 'EIS expected in the second half of 2026' framing. Everything heavier is an unchanged prior-digest carry-forward and is deduplicated out: the NSW Farmers Association's formally carried energy-transition motions (cut the New England REZ from 8GW to 3GW, oppose compulsory acquisition of land for transmission, oblige EnergyCo to reassess all REZ transmission requirements, plus anti-subsidy and baseline soil/water-testing motions) and Rebecca Reardon's presidency; the Coalition's pledge to scrap the New England transmission corridor if elected; Minister Sharpe's $14.5m Central-West Orana Telecommunications Infrastructure Uplift Program; Squadron Energy's 16 July Boorolong exit; the New England Draft REZ Access Scheme Declaration on exhibition (feedback by 6 August, declaration targeted end-September, energisation targeted 2032); the refined 1km Muswellbrook-Walcha corridor and its July-September field-investigation program across roughly 150 affected landholders amid Walcha High Country Guardians opposition and the 22,000-signature petition; EnergyCo's 15 July South West REZ Project Development Deed with Transgrid (Jerilderie-Wagga Wagga, unlocking 3.56GW); the South West REZ $60m Community and Employment Benefit Program consultation (3 August webinar, drop-in sessions at Jerilderie and Coleambally on 12 August and Darlington Point on 20 August); the Illawarra REZ Community Reference Group call; and on Central-West Orana the Port-to-REZ OSOM delivery campaign with turbine-blade deliveries to Uungula underway this month, the Main Road No. 709 gazettal and ACEREZ's staged access-track works under stronger heritage controls with the DPHI rock-shelter assessment still open, plus the community roadshow flagged for 11-15 August. Source gaps to log rather than read as absence of news: ABC News, The Guardian Australia and the paid mastheads (AFR, SMH, the ACM regional titles) surfaced no new dated REZ headline in this run even at standfirst level, so no paywalled items are carried today. Nothing in the scan changes the standing posture: the dominant exposures remain the New England political and social-licence contest ahead of the March 2027 state election, and the delivery and heritage risks on Central-West Orana.

items.headline: EnergyCo opens consultation on the New England REZ $60m community benefit fund
items.summary: EnergyCo has launched formal consultation on how to design and deliver the New England Renewable Energy Zone's Community and Employment Benefit Program, an initial $60 million in legacy benefits for the region, inviting residents, councils and First Nations groups to take part through July and August via an online survey, a webinar and community sessions. The funding is being brought forward so projects can begin before REZ construction starts, following the pattern set in the Central-West Orana REZ, where the same scheme has backed worker accommodation, water-security work and early education services; EnergyCo puts the New England REZ at more than 6,000 construction jobs and 2,000 ongoing operational jobs.
items.so_what: This is EnergyCo's clearest social-licence lever yet in the most politically contested zone, deliberately front-loading a visible local dividend into New England while the Coalition campaigns to scrap the transmission corridor, the NSW Farmers' 8GW-to-3GW motion stands, and Walcha opposition and the 22,000-signature petition harden ahead of the March 2027 state election. Whether the consultation is read as genuine benefit-sharing or as a sweetener will shape community sentiment, so it is worth tracking submission volumes, First Nations engagement and how host towns versus the wider region are treated in the funding design.

items.headline: ACEREZ to open Round 2 of its Central-West Orana community grants on 10 August
items.summary: ACEREZ, the ACCIONA-COBRA-Endeavour consortium building the Central-West Orana REZ transmission network, has confirmed that Round 2 of its Community Grants Program will open on 10 August with roughly $1.9 million available, offering small grants of $3,000-$50,000 and significant grants of $50,000-$1 million to not-for-profits, Aboriginal organisations, councils and volunteer groups. The program is a multi-year initiative delivered in staged rounds through 2028, following a first round that backed 46 local projects across amenities, education, sport, agriculture, health and Indigenous community support.
items.so_what: The grants are a developer-funded goodwill mechanism running alongside EnergyCo's own Central-West Orana benefit spending, and steady, visible local investment helps offset the delivery and heritage friction on the zone — the OSOM turbine-blade deliveries, the access-track works and the still-open DPHI rock-shelter assessment. Grant uptake, the spread of awards across host communities, and any contest over who benefits are worth monitoring as a barometer of Central-West Orana social licence as construction intensifies.
